cells.A2: Built 17 Oct 2026 from the full Python model (model/cohort_engine.py) at the agreed likely values (Assumptions tab). Metric: undiscounted cumulative P&L. Round 8 (17 Oct): sign-ups 100 a month in year 1, falling in a straight line to 70% of that by month 49; half of onboardings start as bought online leads (₹250 each) and are served offline like any saver; the old +10% a year sign-up growth is gone. Round 9 (17 Oct): the loan origination fee starts at a DSA's rate (1.75%) and rises in a straight line to 1.5x by company month 60 (Monthly column Z); home loans and LAP unchanged. Round 10 (17 Oct): the agent's 0.25% pay on balance is capped at ₹10,000 a month (incentive_cap).
cells.A5: Change the blue cells in column B of Inputs. Per saver, Monthly and Summary recalculate. Low and high are the agreed range.
cells.A6: Grey cells at the bottom of Inputs are worked out from the blue ones; do not type there. Do not type on Per saver or Monthly.
cells.A7: Summary column B is live; column C is the full Python model at the likely values and does not move, so the gap shows how far your change has moved the answer (plus the toy's own small error at the likely values, shown in column F).
cells.A10: Inputs: the 51 inputs (blue), 6 rarely-changed ones and the worked-out values. Every input has a name used in the formulas.
cells.A11: Per saver: one sign-up's months 1-60 (his age): still saving, deposits, fund balance, UPI and cash visits, fund trail, loans (never borrowed, back in the pool after repaying, applications, first and repeat loans, money lent), top-ups, cards, cross-sell, home loans and LAP, collections and running cost. Calendar year 1 terms.
cells.A12: Monthly: months 1-60. Each total line is one formula: the sum over every month's sign-ups of the Per saver line at their age (MMULT of a 60 x 60 cohort matrix with the sign-ups), times the calendar-year growth factor for that line. Then revenue, costs, net and cumulative P&L.
cells.A13: Summary: cumulative P&L at 12, 36 and 60 months, payback month, peak cash need, year-5 savers, money lent and loans, revenue per active saver, and where the money comes from.
cells.A14: Assumptions, Monte Carlo, Sign-ups, Agent pay, Sensitivity: pasted values from the full Python model, run 17 Oct 2026 (Monte Carlo: 10,000 draws, seed 20261016). They do not change when you edit Inputs.
cells.A16: The toy is a simplification of the full model
cells.A17: 1. Calendar growth. Take-up (+5% a year) and approval (+10% a year) grow by calendar year. The full model gives every month's sign-ups its own profile; the toy computes one profile in year-1 terms and multiplies each month's total by that month's factor. Exact for anything booked at take-up (cards, home loans, LAP, first loans) apart from item 2.
cells.A18: 2. Never-borrowed pool. With growth, savers borrow sooner, so the pool who never borrowed empties faster. Monthly column J corrects the loan lines for it (1 = no growth). With growth set to 0 the toy's loans, top-ups, cards and housing equal the full model's exactly.
cells.A19: 3. Top-ups (13-35 months after the loan) take the loan factor of 20 months earlier; collections that of 12 months earlier.
cells.A20: 4. Collections: one fee per loan made (31-90 days late and 90+ days bad, ₹170.77), paid 12 months after the loan; the full model pays the two parts after 9 and 18 months.
cells.A21: 5. The 17 non-housing products (insurance, SIP, NPS, FD, gold, recharge, bills, gold / consumer / vehicle loans) are one input, ₹106.0 per active saver a year in his first year saved, growing 20% for each full year he has saved (xs_growth), calibrated to the full model's 60-month money. The full model's money builds up with years saved product by product (renewals, holdings); the 20% step tracks it: the toy is within about ₹0.6k of it at month 36 and pays back in the same month. At 0% growth the toy books cross-sell evenly and runs about ₹42k ahead at month 36.
cells.A22: 6. Repeat loans (0.2% of loans) take the first-loan factor. Home loans and LAP are modelled as in the full model.

cells.A44: Company tabs: THE BASE (final; tables/base_*, model/base_plan.py): 30% of personal-loan volume on our own NBFC book from month 30, and the real-world city limits
cells.A45: The plan: 172 cities opened in rank order (City plan tab), 300 agents by month 18, then +150 a month, capped at 5,000; each city's sign-ups slow as it fills: x (1 - (cumulative / cap)^2), cap = 20% of the city's urban self-employed pool, growing 3% a year; the central team as built; funding = the rounds table: Seed ₹13 crore at month 0; A ₹53 crore at month 9; B ₹212 crore at month 18; C ₹605 crore at month 32; D ₹215 crore at month 48; E ₹10 crore at month 57; 96 company months.
cells.A46: Tabs: Company inputs (fleet path as a check, cities, costs, NBFC, the ROUNDS table; blue). City plan: 172 cities (blue: city, rank, addressable, launch month, agents at each tenure point) with each city's penetration and slowdown at months 60 and 96. City by month: 96 months x 172 cities (agents, new books, sign-ups before the slowdown, the cap, cumulative sign-ups, sign-ups). Company per book, Company monthly (the company's agents and sign-ups are summed from the cities; NBFC lines: on-book loans, book, interest, cost of funds, NII, processing fees, provisions, equity, borrowings), Company yearly (years 1-8), Funding & cap table (cap table; the three lenses at month 60), Company summary.
cells.A47: Every city is modelled individually (no aggregate): the slowdown runs row by row over the 96 months, vectorised across the 172 cities. Each book's agent works at the fleet's average sign-up level (agent_level, the agreed distribution's mean, 1.017 x the likely 100). The per-book costs (capped pay on balance, helpers, cash cover) use the average book of each age, scaled by the company's ratio of saturated to unsaturated balance, visits and cash (one ratio for all cities: an approximation). The NBFC as the full model (nbfc.py): EMIs at the 26% yield over 36 months, provisions of 0.6 x the agreed 3% loss at disbursal, equity = the larger of ₹10 crore NOF and 25% of the book, borrowings the rest at 13.5%.
cells.A48: The unicorn check (Funding & cap table): lens 1 = 20 x ARR (ARR = 12 x month-60 fees + NII + processing fees), lens 2 = 0.45 x AUM, both against ₹10,000 crore; lens 3 (cross-check) = 3 x NBFC equity + 20 x fee ARR. All multiples are OUR JUDGEMENT and blue inputs there.
cells.A49: Where the toy and the full model part: the full model opens cities AUTOMATICALLY (each hire to the city with the most headroom); the City plan records that rollout at tenure points, and its straight lines put about 7.5% more agents in year 2. The full model run on the same City plan gives year-2 revenue +9.2% and year-5 EBITDA -₹9.0 crore (vs -₹7.9 crore AUTO); the toy is within 1% of that run's revenue in every year.
cells.A50: Earlier plan 2, kept for reference: the unicorn track (no NBFC, no city limits): 300 agents by month 18, +200 a month, cap 7,500; rounds ₹1,308 crore by month 60. Full model: year-5 revenue ₹577 crore, year-5 EBITDA ₹-218 crore; the toy matched it within 1.7% on revenue and 0.8% on EBITDA in years 1-5 (tables/unicorn_toy_vs_full.csv).
